transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-15 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Redwood), Aisha Khan (Stratus - Head of ML), Tom Rivers (Stratus - Cloud Architect), Marta Silva (Stratus - Security PM), Jamal Edwards (Stratus - SRE)

Summary (auto): Quick console walkthrough focusing on usage analytics per-route, cost breakdown by model and route, and security/Qs re: private deployments and KMS. Agreed to run pilot and exchange docs.

[00:00] Lena: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, really appreciate it. I'm Lena, I'm the AE on this account, with Diego our SE and Maya from solutions. How's everyone doing?
[00:07] Aisha: Doing good, thanks. Excited to see the console walkthrough — we want to understand cost/levers before committing to anything.
[00:15] Diego: Great, we'll jump into the console. Quick agenda: per-route dashboards, usage analytics, token-level cost breakdowns, and then a brief look at routing policies and dedicated capacity considerations.
[00:25] Tom: We're primarily interested in per-route performance — we have chat flows, document ingestion embeddings, and a reranking route.
[00:32] Diego: Perfect. Sharing my screen now — apologies if auto-resize kicks in, this is Redwood Console demo tenant.
[00:40] Speaker 1: (background) oh wow
[00:43] Diego: Cool — first up is the usage analytics landing. You can see total token usage trends by day, but importantly you can filter by route. So here's the chat route, you can see tokens in, tokens out, and average latency.
[00:58] Aisha: That latency graph, is that p95 or p99?
[01:02] Diego: It's p95 by default, but you can switch to p99. We also show tail latency under advanced metrics. The per-route breakdown shows model version used per route, and also the quantization profile if you enable it.
[01:18] Lena: On the right there's a cost breakdown pane — we estimate token cost per route based on your selected model and quant profile. This is a predictive estimate — you can also export exact token billing if you're on hosted.
[01:32] Marta: On the security side, does that export include any PII? We need to ensure exports are scrubbed and that audit logs are available.
[01:40] Maya: Good question. Exports respect your retention and redaction settings; we can configure exports to be admin-only and redacted. We also emit audit logs to your SIEM via our export lambda or to your S3 in VPC.
[01:53] Jamal: And keys? We need HSM-level KMS integration.
[01:56] Diego: Yes we support customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations. For Private deployments we can integrate with on-prem HSMs; for Redwood Dedicated you'll get KMS integration in your VPC.
[02:06] Aisha: Back to cost — how accurate are these per-route estimates? Our concern is that batch effects can skew per-call numbers.
[02:14] Diego: Right — we model estimated cost using observed batching and KV cache hits. The console shows both raw per-request token math and an adjusted view that accounts for caching and batching. For example, if a route benefits from prefix caching, the effective tokens billed drop significantly — you'll see that in the adjusted column.
[02:33] Tom: Can we set different SLOs per route? Chat needs 200ms p95, embeddings can be bulk and tolerate higher latency.
[02:42] Lena: Absolutely. Per-route SLOs and routing policies allow you to choose latency vs cost tradeoffs. You can route critical routes to Dedicated capacity and background jobs to hosted lower-cost models.
[02:55] Aisha: Do you have historical cost attribution by feature so we can tie to product metrics?
[03:01] Diego: Yes, the analytics export maps routes to tags/feature keys. You can instrument SDK calls with route tags and then the console aggregates cost per feature.
[03:12] Speaker 2: Sorry quick question
[03:14] Diego: Sure.
[03:16] Tom: On quantization — what's the recommended profile for chat? 4-bit, 8-bit? Any regressions?
[03:22] Maya: We typically recommend 4-bit quant for cost-first scenarios but run evals for quality-sensitive runs. Redwood Optimize will suggest quant profiles based on your eval set and can flag regressions with example prompts.
[03:36] Aisha: Can Optimize hook into our existing eval harness? We run unit prompts and red-team style tests.
[03:42] Diego: Yes, you can upload eval sets or point to a repo; it will run comparisons and produce diffs. We can also kick off a small experiment during the POC.
[03:53] Lena: Jumping back to the dashboard — here's the per-route token waterfall. You can click a route and see contributor factors: prompt tokens, response tokens, cache hits, and batched tokens.
[04:08] Aisha: Nice. That will help us justify Dedicated for the chat route.
[04:12] Diego: Exactly. The cost model will show projected monthly spend under different QPS and batching assumptions. You can toggle model variants — e.g., open-source 70B quantized vs a smaller hosted variant — and see cost and latency projections side-by-side.
[04:28] Marta: On the compliance front, if we go Private or Dedicated, do you run in our VPC? How are logs handled?
[04:35] Maya: For Private we deploy the control plane to your environment and data plane in your VPC; audit logs can be forwarded to your SIEM, and keys stay on your KMS. For Dedicated it's a managed instance with a private network link and customer isolation.
[04:49] Jamal: Any experience with bank workloads and encryption-at-rest policies?
[04:53] Diego: We routinely work with regulated customers; we have SOC 2 Type II and are working toward ISO. We can provide architecture diagrams for your compliance team.
[05:02] Aisha: Great. Let's talk about pilot specifics — what do you need from us?
[05:07] Lena: Ideally a representative workload: sample prompts, typical QPS, and a few critical routes. We'll spin up a demo tenant, run the POC for two weeks, and surface per-route dashboards and a benchmark report.
[05:18] Tom: We'll need to know data residency — some of our data cannot leave region.
[05:22] Maya: We have region pinning for hosted and can run Private in your preferred region. We'll note that as a requirement for the pilot.
[05:29] Speaker 3: (inaudible)
[05:32] Diego: Switching now to the cost-breakdown report — this is the export you'll get. It includes daily token totals, per-route breakdown, model and quant profile used, and an estimated cost column. Note the adjusted cost column which factors in caching and batching.
[05:48] Aisha: In your experience what's the delta between raw and adjusted? Like percent usually?
[05:54] Diego: It varies: for chat routes with heavy prefix reuse, we've seen adjusted be 30-60% lower than raw. For embedding-only routes less caching benefit, maybe 5-15% difference.
[06:06] Lena: We'll include conservative and optimistic scenarios in the cost model we send.
[06:11] Marta: On governance, can we set RBAC so only certain roles can change routing or model pins?
[06:16] Diego: Yes, full RBAC for console actions, and SAML/SSO integration so you can map to your IdP groups.
[06:24] Tom: For the POC, how do you measure quality regressions? We can't accept degraded answers.
[06:30] Maya: Redwood Optimize will run your eval prompts and compare metrics like exact-match, BLEU-ish metrics where relevant, and produce example-level diffs. We can set alert thresholds that block a rollout if quality drops.
[06:42] Aisha: Can we run the Optimize job against our own holdout test set in the pilot?
[06:46] Diego: Yes — we'd recommend shipping a small set of 200-500 prompts to start.
[06:50] Speaker 1: hmm
[06:52] Lena: We're hitting a few questions — want to make sure we get the next steps captured. I'll send the pricing and cost model, Diego will export the per-route CSV, and Maya will share the security pack including SOC 2 artifacts.
[07:05] Tom: For pricing — show us hosted per-token and dedicated reserve pricing. We want a delta for 3-month and 12-month commits.
[07:13] Lena: Yep, we'll include committed discounts and burst options. Also include an example of how quantization and batching change the per-1000-token bill.
[07:23] Aisha: Any public benchmarks you can share for latency on N/A NVidia A100 vs H100? We're planning hardware in our internal R&D.
[07:31] Diego: We have benchmark sheets; I'll share the latency/throughput ranges per GPU family. Keep in mind kernelization/compilation differences and sequence lengths — we'll model your expected seq lens in the POC.
[07:45] Marta: Logging question again — for audit trails do you have immutable logs?
[07:49] Maya: We provide append-only audit streams and can push to your WORM storage if required. We'll include these details in the security packet.
[07:58] Aisha: Sounds good. Any blockers on our side to start the pilot?
[08:02] Lena: Mainly access and a signed NDAs for sample data if you want us to use sensitive data. For non-sensitive testing we can get started right away.
[08:10] Tom: We'll prepare sample traffic and a small eval set.
[08:14] Jamal: Also need to confirm network egress rules — some subnets disallow outbound.
[08:18] Diego: We can support private peering or a data plane in your VPC. We'll document networking options.
[08:24] Speaker 2: (minor crosstalk)
[08:28] Lena: Final recap: send pricing + cost scenarios, per-route CSV, SOC2/security pack, schedule security deep-dive next week, and set up pilot kickoff.
[08:37] Aisha: Thanks — that works.
[08:40] Diego: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with calendar invites.
[08:43] Maya: I'll drop the security docs into the CRM ticket.
[08:46] Tom: Appreciate it.
